A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a model of the nucleons partonic structure that is based on the pion cloud picture, but with the important restriction that the model is only applicable in the region of transverse distances where chiral symmetry is broken, i.e. for transverse distances larger than the pion Compton wavelength.

chiral dynamics and large-distance effects in the nucleon are essential ingredients in the description of its partonic structure, and that the pion cloud picture is valid only at momentum fractions x (1/Mπ) and transverse distances (1/Mπ), and only if one takes into account the physical core radius of the nucleon.
chiral dynamics is a very important component in the nucleon’s structure at low momentum fractions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the partonic structure of the nucleon at large distances (small transverse momenta) is dominated by chiral dynamics, with the pion exchange providing the leading contribution.
chiral dynamics generates a large-distance component of the nucleon's parton distributions, which can be calculated from the physical core radius of the nucleon.
